hook.convey: one whole shared into EQUAL parts → each part gets a name from how many equal parts the whole has: 4 equal parts → 1/4; a roti shared at home, a paper strip folded for a drawing

use.hi: Kitchen mein ek garam roti 4 bachchon mein barabar baantni hai. Har bachche ko jo tukda milta hai, uska ek pakka naam hota hai, aur woh naam roti ke barabar hisson se banta hai.
use.en: A hot roti in the kitchen is to be shared equally among 4 children. The piece each child gets has a proper name, and that name comes from the roti's equal parts.

use.hi: Drawing ke liye kaagaz ki ek lambi patti ko 3 barabar hisson mein mod do aur ek hissa colour karo. Woh rangin hissa patti ka ek fractional unit hai.
use.en: For a drawing, fold a long paper strip into 3 equal parts and colour one part. That coloured part is one fractional unit of the strip.

explain.convey: roti in 4 equal parts → one part = 1/4 = one of 4 equal parts = a fractional unit; the bottom number = how many equal parts the whole has; a same-size roti in 8 equal parts beside it → the child names its unit

point.hi: Yeh roti 4 barabar hisson mein bati hai. Ek hissa poori roti ka 1/4 hai, ek-chauthaai. 1/4 ek fractional unit hai: poore ke 4 barabar hisson mein se ek. Bagal mein utni hi badi doosri roti hai.
point.en: This roti is in 4 equal parts. One part is 1/4 of the whole roti, one quarter. 1/4 is a fractional unit: one of the 4 equal parts of the whole. Beside it is a second roti of the same size.

prompt.hi: Bagal wali roti 8 barabar hisson mein bati hai. Uska ek hissa poori roti ka kaunsa fractional unit hai?
prompt.en: The roti beside it is in 8 equal parts. Which fractional unit of the whole roti is one of its parts?

why.hi: pehli roti 4 hisson mein; yeh roti 8 barabar hisson mein bati, toh ek hissa 1/8 hai
why.en: the first roti is in 4 parts; this one is in 8 equal parts, so one part is 1/8

simpler.hi: Roti 4 barabar hisson mein bati hai, toh ek hissa 1/4 hai. Neeche ka number batata hai ki kitne barabar hisse hain.
simpler.en: The roti is in 4 equal parts, so one part is 1/4. The bottom number tells how many equal parts there are.

explain.convey: two 12 cm strips, both in 3 pieces: A = 4, 4, 4 cm → each piece is 1/3; B = 6, 3, 3 cm → not equal → three pieces alone do not make thirds; 1/3 of 12 cm = 4 cm and no B piece is 4 cm → a piece is 1/3 only if its length is exactly 1/3 of the whole

point.hi: Dono pattiyan 12 cm ki hain, aur dono ke 3 hisse hain. Patti A ke hisse 4 cm, 4 cm, 4 cm hain, sab barabar, toh wahan har hissa 1/3 hai. Patti B ke hisse 6 cm, 3 cm, 3 cm hain, barabar nahi, toh sirf 3 hisse hone se har hissa 1/3 nahi ban jaata. 12 cm ka 1/3 toh 4 cm hai, aur B ka koi hissa 4 cm ka nahi.
point.en: Both strips are 12 cm, and both have 3 pieces. Strip A's pieces are 4 cm, 4 cm, 4 cm, all equal, so there each piece is 1/3. Strip B's pieces are 6 cm, 3 cm, 3 cm, not equal, so having 3 pieces does not make each piece 1/3. 1/3 of 12 cm is 4 cm, and no piece of B is 4 cm.

prompt.hi: Ek aur patti 15 cm ki hai, uske 3 hisse 6 cm, 5 cm aur 4 cm ke hain. Kis hisse ki lambai poori patti ki lambai ka theek 1/3 hai: 6 cm, 5 cm ya 4 cm wale ki?
prompt.en: Another strip is 15 cm, and its 3 pieces are 6 cm, 5 cm and 4 cm. Which piece's length is exactly 1/3 of the whole strip's length: the 6 cm, 5 cm or 4 cm one?

why.hi: 15 ÷ 3 = 5, toh 15 cm ka 1/3 5 cm hai
why.en: 15 ÷ 3 = 5, so 1/3 of 15 cm is 5 cm

simpler.hi: Patti A ke teeno hisse 4 cm ke hain, barabar, isliye har hissa 1/3 hai. Patti B ke hisse barabar nahi, isliye unhe 1/3 nahi keh sakte.
simpler.en: All three pieces of strip A are 4 cm, equal, so each is 1/3. Strip B's pieces are not equal, so they are not 1/3.

explain.convey: a fraction is always of some whole: ribbon P 20 cm → 1/2 = 10 cm; ribbon Q 12 cm → 1/2 = 6 cm; same name, different amount, because the wholes differ

point.hi: Ribbon P 20 cm ki hai, uska 1/2 hai 10 cm. Ribbon Q 12 cm ki hai, uska 1/2 hai 6 cm. Dono hisson ka naam 1/2 hai, par poora alag hai, isliye naam ek, lambai alag.
point.en: Ribbon P is 20 cm, and its 1/2 is 10 cm. Ribbon Q is 12 cm, and its 1/2 is 6 cm. Both pieces are called 1/2, but the wholes are different, so same name, different length.

prompt.hi: Ab dono ribbon ka 1/4 lo. Ribbon P ka 1/4, ribbon Q ke 1/4 se kitne cm lamba hai?
prompt.en: Now take 1/4 of both ribbons. How many cm longer is 1/4 of ribbon P than 1/4 of ribbon Q?

why.hi: ribbon P: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm; ribbon Q: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 cm; 5 − 3 = 2
why.en: ribbon P: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm; ribbon Q: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 cm; 5 − 3 = 2

simpler.hi: P aur Q dono ka 1/2 lete hain, par P lambi ribbon hai. Isliye P ka 1/2 bhi lamba hai, naam ek, lambai alag.
simpler.en: We take 1/2 of both P and Q, but P is the longer ribbon. So P's 1/2 is longer too: same name, different length.

problem.hi: 30 cm lamba ek ganna 5 barabar tukdon mein toda gaya. Ek tukda poore ganne ka kaunsa fraction hai, aur woh kitna lamba hai?
problem.en: A sugarcane 30 cm long is broken into 5 equal pieces. What fraction of the whole sugarcane is one piece, and how long is it?

givens.en: the sugarcane is in 5 equal pieces

find.hi: ek tukde ka fractional unit aur uski lambai
find.en: the fractional unit for one piece and its length

do.hi: Dekho poora ganna kitne barabar tukdon mein bata hai
do.en: See how many equal pieces the whole sugarcane is in

why.hi: ganna 5 barabar tukdon mein bata hai aur yeh unmein se ek hai
why.en: the sugarcane is in 5 equal pieces and this is one of them

simpler.hi: Ganna 5 barabar tukdon mein hai. Ek tukda unmein se ek hai, yaani ganne ka 1/5.
simpler.en: The sugarcane is in 5 equal pieces. One piece is one of those, so it is 1/5 of the sugarcane.

do.hi: Ek tukde ki lambai ke liye poori lambai ko 5 se bhaag do
do.en: For one piece's length, divide the whole length by 5

why.hi: saare tukde barabar hain, toh 30 cm sab mein barabar batta hai
why.en: all the pieces are equal, so the 30 cm is shared equally among them

simpler.hi: Saare tukde barabar hain. Isliye 30 cm ko 5 barabar hisson mein baanto: 30 ÷ 5.
simpler.en: All the pieces are equal. So share the 30 cm into 5 equal parts: 30 ÷ 5.

prompt.hi: Ab 30 ÷ 5 nikalo. Ek tukda kitne cm lamba hai?
prompt.en: Now work out 30 ÷ 5. How many cm long is one piece?

simpler.hi: 5 ko kis number se guna karein ki 30 aaye, woh number dhoondo.
simpler.en: Find the number that, times 5, makes 30.

why.hi: 30 ÷ 5 = 6, toh 5 barabar tukdon mein har tukda 6 cm ka hai
why.en: 30 ÷ 5 = 6, so each of the 5 equal pieces is 6 cm

answer.hi: ek tukda poore ganne ka 1/5 hai aur 6 cm lamba hai
answer.en: one piece is 1/5 of the whole sugarcane and is 6 cm long

why.hi: 1/5 ka matlab hai 5 barabar hisson mein se ek, aur 5 tukde × 6 cm = 30 cm, yaani poora ganna
why.en: 1/5 means one of 5 equal parts, and 5 pieces × 6 cm = 30 cm, the whole sugarcane

prompt.hi: 16 cm ki ek chocolate bar ke tukde 6 cm, 6 cm, 2 cm aur 2 cm ke hain. Inmein se kitne tukde bar ka 1/4 hain?
prompt.en: A 16 cm chocolate bar breaks into pieces of 6 cm, 6 cm, 2 cm and 2 cm. How many of these pieces are 1/4 of the bar?

why.hi: chocolate bar 16 cm ka 1/4 = 4 cm; tukde 6, 6, 2, 2 cm hain, koi 4 cm nahi, yaani 0
why.en: 1/4 of 16 cm is 4 cm, and no piece is 4 cm, so 0

simpler.hi: Pehle 16 cm ka 1/4 nikalo. Phir dekho kaunse tukde theek utne lambe hain.
simpler.en: First find 1/4 of 16 cm. Then see which pieces are exactly that long.

prompt.hi: Ek ribbon 60 cm ki hai aur doosri 30 cm ki. Rahul ne pehli ribbon ka 1/3 liya, Sana ne doosri ka 1/3. Rahul ka tukda Sana ke tukde se kitne cm lamba hai?
prompt.en: One ribbon is 60 cm and another is 30 cm. Rahul took 1/3 of the first ribbon, Sana took 1/3 of the second. How many cm longer is Rahul's piece than Sana's?

why.hi: Rahul: 60 ÷ 3 = 20 cm, Sana: 30 ÷ 3 = 10 cm ribbon, aur 20 − 10 = 10
why.en: Rahul's 1/3 is 60 ÷ 3 = 20 cm, Sana's 30 ÷ 3 = 10 cm, and 20 − 10 = 10

simpler.hi: 60 cm ka 1/3 aur 30 cm ka 1/3 alag-alag nikalo. Phir bade tukde mein se chhota ghatao.
simpler.en: Find 1/3 of 60 cm and 1/3 of 30 cm separately. Then take the smaller piece away from the bigger one.

ladder.why: first naming: a roti in 4 equal pieces → one piece = 1/4, as on the e1 board
quick retrieval with a new count: 6 equal parts → unit 1/6
make 1/3 on a paper strip → the parts must be EQUAL before one is shaded
half of a big vs half of a small pizza → same fraction, different whole, different amount
harder: 1 litre in 125 mL pots → find how many equal parts first, then the unit 1/8

remediation.move: equal-thirds strip beside the broken bar: lay each piece against one third of the strip → only pieces that match one third exactly carry the name 1/3; 1 big + 2 small never match

say.hi: Koi tukda 1/3 tabhi hai jab uski lambai poore ki theek 1/3 ho. Sirf tukde gin lene se 1/3 nahi banta. Pehle poori lambai ko 3 se bhaag do, phir utni lambai wala tukda dhoondo.
say.en: A piece is 1/3 only if its length is exactly 1/3 of the whole. Just counting the pieces does not make thirds. First divide the whole length by 3, then find the piece of that length.

simpler.hi: Poori lambai ko 3 se bhaag do. Sirf theek utni lambai wala tukda 1/3 hai.
simpler.en: Divide the whole length by 3. Only a piece of exactly that length is 1/3.

prompt.hi: 18 cm ki ribbon ke 3 tukde 8 cm, 6 cm aur 4 cm ke hain. Kaunsa tukda poori ribbon ka theek 1/3 hai: 8, 6 ya 4 cm?
prompt.en: An 18 cm ribbon has pieces of 8 cm, 6 cm and 4 cm. Which piece is exactly 1/3 of the whole ribbon: 8, 6 or 4 cm?

why.hi: ribbon 18 cm ka 1/3 = 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cm; 3 tukde mein 8 aur 4 cm wale nahi
why.en: 1/3 of the 18 cm ribbon is 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cm; the 8 cm and 4 cm pieces are not

simpler.hi: 18 cm ko 3 se bhaag do, yaani 18 ÷ 3. Jo tukda utna lamba ho, wahi 1/3 hai.
simpler.en: Divide 18 cm by 3, that is 18 ÷ 3. The piece that long is the 1/3.

remediation.move: two strips of different lengths, each folded in half, the small half laid on the big half → 'half' depends on the whole it is half of; same name, different length

say.hi: 1/3 ka matlab hai apne poore ke 3 barabar hisson mein se ek. Lambi ribbon ka 1/3 lamba hota hai, chhoti ribbon ka 1/3 chhota. Naam ek hi hai, par poora alag, toh lambai bhi alag.
say.en: 1/3 means one of 3 equal parts of its own whole. A long ribbon has a long 1/3, a short ribbon a short 1/3. The name is the same, but the whole is different, so the length is different too.

simpler.hi: Har ribbon ka 1/3 alag se nikalo. Phir dono lambaiyon ko milao.
simpler.en: Find 1/3 of each ribbon on its own. Then compare the two lengths.

prompt.hi: Ribbon A 36 cm ki hai, ribbon B 18 cm ki. A ka 1/3, B ke 1/3 se kitne cm lamba hai?
prompt.en: Ribbon A is 36 cm, ribbon B is 18 cm. How many cm longer is 1/3 of A than 1/3 of B?

why.hi: ribbon A: 36 ÷ 3 = 12 cm, ribbon B: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cm, aur 12 − 6 = 6
why.en: ribbon A: 36 ÷ 3 = 12 cm, ribbon B: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cm, and 12 − 6 = 6

simpler.hi: 36 cm ka 1/3 aur 18 cm ka 1/3 alag-alag nikalo. Phir bade mein se chhota ghatao.
simpler.en: Find 1/3 of 36 cm and 1/3 of 18 cm separately. Then take the smaller from the bigger.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak humne ek poore ko barabar hisson mein baanta aur har hisse ko naam diya. Agle hisse mein ek hi poore ko kam ya zyada barabar hisson mein baant kar hisson ki tulna karenge.
bridgeToNext.en: So far we shared one whole into equal parts and named each part. Next we will split one whole into fewer or more equal parts and compare the parts.

hook.convey: the same cake shared by 3 friends or by 6 friends; the same train route split into parts → compare one share from each; same whole, more equal parts → each part smaller

use.hi: Ek birthday cake 3 dost barabar baant rahe hain, aur bilkul waisa hi doosra cake 6 dost. Aaj dekhenge ki kis cake mein ek dost ka tukda bada hai.
use.en: Three friends are sharing a birthday cake equally, and six friends are sharing another cake exactly like it. Today we see in which cake one friend's piece is bigger.

use.hi: Ek hi train route par Rahul route ka ek hissa safar karta hai aur Sana ek doosra hissa. Route ek hi hai, isliye dono hisson ki tulna ho sakti hai.
use.en: On the same train route, Rahul travels one part of the route and Sana another part. The route is the same, so the two parts can be compared.

explain.convey: one 0-to-1 line in 6 equal parts: first mark = 1/6; the same line in 3 equal parts would end its first part at the second mark, 2/6 = 1/3 → 6 is the bigger number but 1/6 is the smaller part

point.hi: Yeh 0 se 1 ki line 6 barabar hisson mein bati hai, toh 0 ke baad pehla nishaan 1/6 hai. Agar wahi line sirf 3 barabar hisson mein bati hoti, toh pehla hissa doosre nishaan tak jaata, jahan likha hai 2/6 = 1/3. 6 bada number hai, par 1/6 chhota hissa hai.
point.en: This 0-to-1 line has 6 equal parts, so the first mark after 0 is 1/6. If the same line were in only 3 equal parts, the first part would reach the second mark, where it says 2/6 = 1/3. 6 is the bigger number, but 1/6 is the smaller part.

prompt.hi: Agar wahi 0 se 1 sirf 2 barabar hisson mein bate, toh kaunsa hissa lamba hoga: 1/2 ya 1/6?
prompt.en: If the same 0 to 1 were split into only 2 equal parts, which part would be longer: 1/2 or 1/6?

why.hi: wahi line kam hisson mein bate toh hissa lamba hota hai; 2 hisse 6 se kam, isliye 1/2 = 3/6 lamba
why.en: fewer parts of the same line means longer parts; 2 parts are fewer than 6, so 1/2 = 3/6 is longer

simpler.hi: Line 6 barabar hisson mein hai, toh ek hissa 1/6 hai. Jitne kam hisse, utna lamba har hissa, isliye 1/3 bada hai.
simpler.en: The line is in 6 equal parts, so one part is 1/6. Fewer parts make each part longer, so 1/3 is bigger.

explain.convey: three same-size chocolate bars shared by 3, 5, 10 friends → each gets 1/3, 1/5, 1/10 → more friends, smaller share → order unit fractions by their bottom numbers, the biggest bottom first when smallest first

point.hi: Yeh teen chocolate bar ek hi size ki hain. Pehli 3 doston mein barabar bati, doosri 5 mein, teesri 10 mein, toh har bar mein utne barabar hisse hain. Zyada dost, chhota hissa.
point.en: These three chocolate bars are the same size. The first is shared equally by 3 friends, the second by 5, the third by 10, so each bar has that many equal parts. More friends, smaller share.

prompt.hi: Isi size ki bar ke 1/3, 1/10 aur 1/5 hisse ko sabse chhote se sabse bade ke kram mein lagao.
prompt.en: Put 1/3, 1/10 and 1/5 of a bar this size in order, from smallest to biggest.

why.hi: zyada barabar hisse matlab chhota hissa hota hai, toh 1/10 sabse chhota, phir 1/5, phir 1/3
why.en: more equal parts means a smaller part, so 1/10 is smallest, then 1/5, then 1/3

simpler.hi: Bar jitne zyada doston mein bate, har dost ka hissa utna chhota. Har bar ke barabar hisse dekho.
simpler.en: The more friends share a bar, the smaller each share. Look at the equal parts of each bar.

problem.hi: Teen ek hi size ki chocolate bar baanti gayi: pehli 6 doston mein barabar, doosri 3 doston mein, aur teesri 8 doston mein. Kis group mein har dost ko sabse bada hissa mila, aur 1/6, 1/3, 1/8 ka sabse bade se sabse chhote tak kram kya hai?
problem.en: Three chocolate bars of the same size are shared: the first equally by 6 friends, the second by 3 friends, and the third by 8 friends. In which group does each friend get the biggest share, and what is the order of 1/6, 1/3, 1/8 from biggest to smallest?

givens.hi: teeno bar ek hi size ki hain
givens.en: all three bars are the same size

givens.hi: pehli bar 6 doston mein, doosri 3 doston mein, teesri 8 doston mein
givens.en: the first bar is shared by 6 friends, the second by 3, the third by 8

find.hi: sabse bade hisse wala group, aur 1/6, 1/3, 1/8 ka kram, sabse bada pehle
find.en: the group with the biggest share, and 1/6, 1/3, 1/8 in order, biggest first

do.hi: Har group mein ek dost ka hissa likho
do.en: Write one friend's share in each group

why.hi: har bar apne group ke doston mein barabar bati hai
why.en: each bar is shared equally among its own group

simpler.hi: Har bar apne group mein barabar bati. Toh 6 doston mein har ek ko 1/6, 3 mein 1/3, aur 8 mein 1/8.
simpler.en: Each bar is shared equally in its own group. So with 6 friends each gets 1/6, with 3 it is 1/3, with 8 it is 1/8.

do.hi: Bar ek hi size ki hain, toh har bar ke barabar hisson ki ginti dekho
do.en: The bars are the same size, so look at the number of equal parts in each

steps.result: 3 doston wali bar sabse kam tukdon mein, 8 doston wali sabse zyada tukdon mein

why.hi: ek hi poore ke jitne kam barabar hisse hon, har hissa utna bada hota hai
why.en: the fewer equal parts the same whole has, the bigger each part is

simpler.hi: Teeno bar ek hi size ki hain. 3 doston wali bar ke sabse kam tukde hain, 8 doston wali ke sabse zyada.
simpler.en: All three bars are the same size. The 3-friend bar has the fewest pieces, the 8-friend bar the most.

why.hi: wahan bar sabse kam hisson mein bati hai
why.en: there the bar is in the fewest parts

simpler.hi: Kam tukde matlab bada tukda. Isliye 3 doston wale group mein har dost ko sabse bada hissa mila.
simpler.en: Fewer pieces means bigger pieces. So in the 3-friend group each friend gets the biggest share.

prompt.hi: Ab 1/6, 1/3 aur 1/8 ko sabse bade se sabse chhote ke kram mein lagao.
prompt.en: Now put 1/6, 1/3 and 1/8 in order from biggest to smallest.

simpler.hi: Jo sabse bada hissa abhi chuna, use pehle likho. Phir yaad rakho, jitne zyada tukde, utna chhota hissa.
simpler.en: Write first the biggest share we just picked. Then remember: the more pieces, the smaller each share.

why.hi: ek hi size ki bar mein 3 hisse sabse bade aur 8 sabse chhote, toh 1/3, 1/6, 1/8
why.en: in same-size bars thirds are biggest and eighths smallest, so 1/3, 1/6, 1/8

answer.hi: 3 doston wale group mein har dost ko sabse bada hissa milta hai, aur kram 1/3, 1/6, 1/8 hai
answer.en: each friend in the group of 3 gets the biggest share, and the order is 1/3, 1/6, 1/8

why.hi: teeno bar barabar size ki hain, aur ek hi poore ke jitne zyada barabar hisse, har hissa utna chhota
why.en: the three bars are the same size, and the more equal parts the same whole has, the smaller each part

prompt.hi: Ek roti 4 doston mein barabar baanti gayi, aur utni hi badi doosri roti 7 doston mein. Kisko zyada roti mili: 4 mein se ek dost ko ya 7 mein se ek dost ko?
prompt.en: One roti is shared equally by 4 friends, and another roti of the same size by 7 friends. Who gets more roti: one of the 4 friends or one of the 7 friends?

why.hi: ek jaisi roti 4 mein bate toh 1/4, 7 mein bate toh 1/7; 1/4 wala hissa bada hota hai
why.en: the same roti shared by 4 gives 1/4, which is bigger than the 1/7 from sharing by 7

simpler.hi: Ek roti 4 barabar hisson mein kati, doosri 7 barabar hisson mein. Kam hisse matlab bade hisse.
simpler.en: One roti is cut into 4 equal parts, the other into 7 equal parts. Fewer parts make bigger parts.

prompt.hi: {friend} ne inhe chhote se bade ke kram mein lagaya: 1/2, 1/3, 1/6, 1/9. Sahi kram kya hai, sabse chhota pehle?
prompt.en: {friend} put these in order from smallest to biggest: 1/2, 1/3, 1/6, 1/9. What is the correct order, smallest first?

why.hi: lagaya kram ulta tha; sahi kram sabse chhota pehle: 9 hisse sabse chhote, toh 1/9, 1/6, 1/3, 1/2
why.en: of one whole, ninths are smallest and halves biggest, so 1/9, 1/6, 1/3, 1/2

simpler.hi: Sab ek hi poore ke hisse hain. Neeche ka number jitna bada, hissa utna chhota, toh sabse bade neeche wale number se shuru karo.
simpler.en: These are all parts of one whole. The bigger the bottom number, the smaller the part, so start with the biggest bottom number.

prompt.hi: Ek hi train route par Rahul ne route ka 1/7 safar kiya aur Sana ne 1/9. Kisne zyada doori tay ki: Rahul ne ya Sana ne?
prompt.en: On the same train route, Rahul travelled 1/7 of the route and Sana 1/9. Who covered more distance: Rahul or Sana?

why.hi: ek hi route ke 7 barabar hisse 9 hisson se bade hote hain, isliye Rahul ka 1/7 Sana ke 1/9 se zyada
why.en: 7 equal parts of the same route are bigger than 9 equal parts, so Rahul's 1/7 is more than Sana's 1/9

simpler.hi: Route ek hi hai: 1/7 matlab saat barabar hisson mein se ek, 1/9 matlab nau mein se ek. Kam hisse karne par har hissa bada hota hai.
simpler.en: It is the same route: 1/7 is one of seven equal parts, 1/9 is one of nine. Fewer parts make each part bigger.

ladder.why: predict from a sharing story: same roti by 3 vs by 5 → one of the 3 gets more
how many 1/4 pieces fill one whole → the bottom number counts the equal pieces of the whole
error-spot: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5 called smallest-first → it is reversed
explain in words why 1/8 < 1/6 though 8 > 6: more equal parts, smaller each
same route, 1/7 vs 1/9 → apply the rule to distance, not food

remediation.move: one 0-to-1 line in 8 equal parts: 1/8 is the first mark, 1/4 = 2/8 the second, so 1/8 sits halfway between 0 and 1/4 → twice the parts, each part half as long → the bigger bottom number gives the shorter piece

say.hi: Ek hi line jitne zyada barabar hisson mein bate, har hissa utna chhota hota hai. Hisse do guna ho jaayein toh har hissa aadha reh jaata hai. Neeche ka bada number chhota hissa deta hai.
say.en: The more equal parts the same line is split into, the shorter each part. Twice as many parts make each part half as long. A bigger bottom number gives a smaller part.

simpler.hi: Wahi line, zyada hisse, toh chhota hissa. Kam hisse, toh lamba hissa.
simpler.en: Same line, more parts, so a shorter part. Fewer parts, so a longer part.

prompt.hi: Wahi 0 se 1 ek baar 5 barabar hisson mein bata aur ek baar 10 mein. Kaunsa hissa lamba hai: 1/5 ya 1/10?
prompt.en: The same 0 to 1 is split once into 5 equal parts and once into 10. Which part is longer: 1/5 or 1/10?

why.hi: wahi line 5 hisson mein bate toh har hissa 10 hisson wale se lamba hota hai, isliye 1/5
why.en: the same line in 5 parts has longer parts than in 10 parts, so 1/5

simpler.hi: Dono baar line wahi hai. Kam hisson mein baantne par har hissa lamba hota hai.
simpler.en: It is the same line both times. Splitting it into fewer parts makes each part longer.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak ek cheez ko kuch logon mein baanta. Agle hisse mein ek se zyada cheezein barabar baantenge, jaise kuch roti kuch bachchon mein, aur har ek ka hissa fraction mein likhenge.
bridgeToNext.en: So far we shared one thing among some people. Next we will share more than one thing equally, like a few rotis among a few children, and write each share as a fraction.

hook.convey: more than one thing shared equally → each share is a fraction: things on top, sharers below; fewer things than sharers → less than one whole each; a metre of ribbon shared → a fraction of a metre, also in cm

use.hi: Kitchen mein 3 roti bachi hain aur 4 bachche khaane baithe hain. Sabko barabar milna hai, par roti bachchon se kam hain, toh har bachche ko poori roti nahi, roti ka ek fraction milega.
use.en: There are 3 rotis left in the kitchen and 4 children sit down to eat. Everyone must get the same, but there are fewer rotis than children, so each child gets not a whole roti but a fraction of one.

use.hi: Drawing class mein colour paper ki 2 lambi pattiyan 3 doston mein barabar baantni hain. Har dost ka hissa ek patti se kam hoga, aur use fraction mein naapenge.
use.en: In drawing class, 2 long strips of colour paper are to be shared equally among 3 friends. Each friend's share will be less than one strip, and we will measure it as a fraction.

explain.convey: 3 rotis among 4 children: every roti into 4 equal parts → each child gets 1/4 from each roti → 3 rotis give 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3/4 roti each

point.hi: 3 roti 4 bachchon mein barabar baantni hain. Har roti ke 4 barabar hisse karo, jaise is roti mein. Har roti se har bachche ko ek hissa, yaani 1/4 milta hai. Teen roti se teen hisse: 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3/4 roti.
point.en: 3 rotis are to be shared equally among 4 children. Make 4 equal parts of each roti, like this roti. From each roti every child gets one part, that is 1/4. Three rotis give three parts: 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3/4 of a roti.

prompt.hi: Ab bachche wahi 4 hain, par roti sirf 2. Har roti ke aise hi 4 barabar hisse karo. Har bachche ko kitni roti milegi?
prompt.en: Now there are the same 4 children, but only 2 rotis. Make 4 equal parts of each roti in the same way. How much roti does each child get?

why.hi: har roti se har bachche ko 1/4 milta hai, aur 2 roti se 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4
why.en: each child gets 1/4 from each roti, and from 2 rotis 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4

simpler.hi: Har roti ke 4 barabar hisse, aur har bachche ko har roti se ek hissa, yaani 1/4. Teen roti se teen hisse milte hain: 3/4.
simpler.en: Each roti has 4 equal parts, and each child gets one part, 1/4, from every roti. Three rotis give three parts: 3/4.

explain.convey: reasonableness: fewer things than sharers → each share less than 1 whole (3 rotis, 4 children → 3/4); more things than sharers → more than 1 (5 laddoos, 2 children → 5/2); things on top, sharers below

point.hi: 3 roti aur 4 bachche: roti kam, bachche zyada, toh har ek ko 3/4, 1 se kam. 5 laddoo aur 2 bachche: laddoo zyada, toh har ek ko 5/2, 1 se zyada. Dono mein upar cheezein, neeche baantne wale. Yeh roti 8 barabar hisson mein bati hai.
point.en: 3 rotis and 4 children: fewer rotis, more children, so each gets 3/4, less than 1. 5 laddoos and 2 children: more laddoos, so each gets 5/2, more than 1. In both, things on top, sharers below. This roti is in 8 equal parts.

prompt.hi: Ab 3 aisi roti 8 bachchon mein barabar baanto. Har bachche ko kitni roti milegi?
prompt.en: Now share 3 rotis like this equally among 8 children. How much roti does each child get?

why.hi: har roti ke 8 hisse karke har bachche ko har roti se 1/8 milta hai, aur 3 roti se 3/8
why.en: with 8 parts in each roti each child gets 1/8 from each roti, and from 3 rotis 3/8

simpler.hi: Upar woh cheezein jo baanti ja rahi hain, neeche baantne wale. 3 roti aur 4 bachche toh 3/4, 5 laddoo aur 2 bachche toh 5/2.
simpler.en: The things being shared go on top, the sharers below. 3 rotis and 4 children give 3/4; 5 laddoos and 2 children give 5/2.

explain.convey: fractions measure lengths: 1 m ribbon in 4 equal parts → one part = 1/4 m; 1 m = 100 cm → 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm

point.hi: Yeh 1 metre ki ribbon hai, 0 se 1 tak. Upar woh 4 barabar hisson mein bati hai, neeche 5 mein. Upar ka ek hissa 1/4 metre hai. 1 metre = 100 cm, toh 1/4 metre = 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm.
point.en: This is a 1 metre ribbon, from 0 to 1. Above it is in 4 equal parts, below in 5. One part above is 1/4 metre. 1 metre has 100 cm, so 1/4 metre = 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm.

prompt.hi: Neeche wahi 1 metre 5 barabar hisson mein bata hai. Ek hissa kitne cm ka hai?
prompt.en: Below, the same 1 metre is in 5 equal parts. How many cm is one part?

why.hi: 1 metre = 100 cm, aur 1/5 metre = 100 ÷ 5 = 20 cm
why.en: 1 metre = 100 cm, and 1/5 metre = 100 ÷ 5 = 20 cm

simpler.hi: 1 metre mein 100 cm hote hain. 4 barabar hisse kiye, toh har hissa 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm.
simpler.en: 1 metre has 100 cm. In 4 equal parts, each part is 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm.

problem.hi: 5 laddoo 3 bachchon mein barabar baante gaye. Har bachche ko kitna laddoo mila?
problem.en: 5 laddoos are shared equally among 3 children. How much does each child get?

find.hi: har bachche ka hissa, laddoo ke fraction mein
find.en: each child's share, as a fraction of a laddoo

do.hi: Har laddoo ke 3 barabar hisse karo
do.en: Make 3 equal parts of every laddoo

why.hi: 3 bachche hain, toh har laddoo se har bachche ko ek hissa mile
why.en: there are 3 children, so every child gets one part from every laddoo

simpler.hi: 3 bachche hain, toh har laddoo ke 3 barabar hisse karo. Har hissa 1/3 laddoo hai.
simpler.en: There are 3 children, so make 3 equal parts of each laddoo. Each part is 1/3 laddoo.

do.hi: Saare hisse jodo: 5 laddoo, har laddoo mein 3 hisse
do.en: Total the parts: 5 laddoos, 3 parts in each

why.hi: har laddoo se 3 hisse bane
why.en: each laddoo gave 3 parts

simpler.hi: Har laddoo se 3 hisse bane, aur laddoo 5 hain. Toh kul 5 × 3 = 15 hisse.
simpler.en: Each laddoo gave 3 parts, and there are 5 laddoos. So there are 5 × 3 = 15 parts in all.

do.en: Share the 15 parts equally among 3 children

why.hi: baantna barabar hai, toh sabko utne hi hisse milte hain
why.en: the sharing is equal, so everyone gets the same number of parts

simpler.hi: 15 hisse 3 bachchon mein barabar baanto. Har bachche ko 15 ÷ 3 = 5 hisse milte hain.
simpler.en: Share the 15 parts equally among 3 children. Each child gets 15 ÷ 3 = 5 parts.

prompt.hi: Har bachche ko 1/3 laddoo wale 5 hisse mile. Yeh kul kitna laddoo hai, fraction mein?
prompt.en: Each child got 5 parts of 1/3 laddoo each. How much laddoo is that in all, as a fraction?

simpler.hi: Har hissa 1/3 laddoo hai aur ek bachche ko 5 hisse mile. Upar hisson ki ginti likho, neeche 3.
simpler.en: Each part is 1/3 laddoo and one child got 5 parts. Write the number of parts on top and 3 below.

why.hi: har hissa 1/3 laddoo hai aur 5 hisse mile, toh 5/3 laddoo
why.en: each part is 1/3 of a laddoo and the child got 5 parts, so 5/3

answer.hi: har bachche ko 5/3 laddoo milta hai, yaani 1 poora laddoo aur 2/3
answer.en: each child gets 5/3 of a laddoo, that is 1 whole laddoo and 2/3 more

why.hi: har bachche ko har laddoo se 1/3 mila aur laddoo 5 the; laddoo bachchon se zyada, isliye hissa 1 se zyada
why.en: each child got 1/3 from each of 5 laddoos; there are more laddoos than children, so the share is over 1

prompt.hi: 2 chikki 3 doston mein barabar baanti gayi. Har dost ko kitni chikki mili?
prompt.en: 2 chikkis are shared equally among 3 friends. How much chikki does each friend get?

why.hi: har chikki se har dost ko 1/3 milta hai, aur 2 chikki se 1/3 + 1/3 = 2/3
why.en: each friend gets 1/3 from each chikki, and from 2 chikkis 1/3 + 1/3 = 2/3

simpler.hi: Har chikki ke 3 barabar hisse karo. Har dost ko har chikki se ek hissa milta hai, ab uske hisse jodo.
simpler.en: Make 3 equal parts of each chikki. Each friend gets one part from every chikki; now add up that friend's parts.

prompt.hi: 5 metre ribbon 4 banners mein barabar baanti gayi. Har banner ko kitne metre ribbon mili?
prompt.en: 5 metres of ribbon are shared equally among 4 banners. How many metres of ribbon does each banner get?

why.hi: ribbon ke har metre se har banner ko 1/4 m milta hai, aur 5 metre se 5/4 m
why.en: each banner gets 1/4 m from each metre of ribbon, and from 5 metres 5/4 m

simpler.hi: Har metre ko 4 barabar hisson mein baanto. Har banner ko har metre se ek hissa milta hai, ab 5 metre ke hisse jodo.
simpler.en: Share each metre into 4 equal parts. Each banner gets one part from every metre; now add the parts from 5 metres.

prompt.hi: 4 roti 6 bachchon mein barabar baanti gayi. {friend} ne likha ki har bachche ko 6/4 roti mili. Sahi hissa kya hai?
prompt.en: 4 rotis are shared equally among 6 children. {friend} wrote that each child got 6/4 of a roti. What is the correct share?

why.hi: baanti jaane wali 4 roti upar aati hain aur 6 bachche neeche, yaani 4/6
why.en: the 4 rotis being shared sit on top and the 6 children below, so 4/6

simpler.hi: Har roti 6 barabar hisson mein kati hai. Jo cheez baanti ja rahi hai woh upar aati hai, aur baantne wale neeche.
simpler.en: Each roti is cut into 6 equal parts. The thing being shared goes on top, and the sharers go below.

ladder.why: the core case: 3 rotis among 4 children → 3/4 each, as in e1
2 chikkis among 3 → 2/3, then judge it against half: is the share sensible
a 1 m ribbon in 4 equal pieces → 1/4 m and 25 cm: fractions as lengths
harder: 7 m among 4 banners → more things than sharers → 7/4 m, more than 1

remediation.move: bar model: each roti drawn as a bar in 5 equal parts, one part per child in every bar → each child 1/5 from each roti → 1/5 + 1/5 = 2/5; fewer rotis than children → share below 1 whole → 5/2 is impossible

say.hi: Roti bachchon se kam hon, toh har hissa 1 se kam hota hai. Har roti ke utne barabar hisse karo jitne bachche hain, aur har bachche ko har roti se ek hissa do. Roti upar, bachche neeche.
say.en: When there are fewer rotis than children, each share is less than 1. Cut every roti into as many equal parts as there are children, and give each child one part from every roti. Rotis on top, children below.

simpler.hi: Roti kam, bachche zyada, toh hissa 1 se kam. Roti upar, bachche neeche.
simpler.en: Fewer rotis than children means a share less than 1. Rotis on top, children below.

prompt.hi: 4 roti 7 bachchon mein barabar baanti gayi. Har bachche ko kitni roti mili?
prompt.en: 4 rotis are shared equally among 7 children. How much roti does each child get?

why.hi: har roti se har bachche ko 1/7 milta hai, aur 4 roti se 4/7
why.en: each child gets 1/7 from each roti, and from 4 rotis 4/7

simpler.hi: Har roti ke 7 barabar hisse karo, aur har bachche ko har roti se ek hissa do. Ab gino, 4 roti se kitne hisse mile.
simpler.en: Make 7 equal parts of each roti, and give each child one part from every roti. Now count the parts from 4 rotis.
